The **Mississippi River**[[b]](#cite_note-25) is the [primary river](/wiki/Main_stem "Main stem") of the largest drainage basin in the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States").[[c]](#cite_note-26)[[24]](#cite_note-27) It is the second-longest river in the United States, behind only the [Missouri](/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River").[[25]](#cite_note-USGSlongest-28) From its traditional source of [Lake Itasca](/wiki/Lake_Itasca "Lake Itasca") in northern [Minnesota](/wiki/Minnesota "Minnesota"), it flows generally south for 2,340 mi (3,766 km)[[25]](#cite_note-USGSlongest-28) to the [Mississippi River Delta](/wiki/Mississippi_River_Delta "Mississippi River Delta") in the [Gulf of Mexico](/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"). With its many [tributaries](/wiki/Tributaries "Tributaries"), the Mississippi's [watershed](/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") drains all or parts of 32 [U.S. states](/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") and two [Canadian provinces](/wiki/Canadian_provinces "Canadian provinces") between the [Rocky](/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") and [Appalachian](/wiki/Appalachian_Mountains "Appalachian Mountains") mountains.[[26]](#cite_note-29) The river either borders or passes through the states of Minnesota, [Wisconsin](/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin"), [Iowa](/wiki/Iowa "Iowa"), [Illinois](/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), [Missouri](/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"), [Kentucky](/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), [Tennessee](/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), [Arkansas](/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas"), [Mississippi](/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"), and [Louisiana](/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana").[[27]](#cite_note-30)[[28]](#cite_note-31) The [main stem](/wiki/Main_stem "Main stem") is entirely within the United States; the total [drainage basin](/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") is 1,151,000 mi2 (2,980,000 km2), of which only about one percent is in Canada. The Mississippi ranks as the world's [tenth-largest river](/wiki/List_of_rivers_by_discharge "List of rivers by discharge") by discharge flow, and the largest in North America.

The OPEC Conference is the supreme authority of the organisation, and consists of delegations normally headed by the oil ministers of member countries. The chief executive of the organisation is the [OPEC secretary general](/wiki/List_of_Secretaries_General_of_OPEC "List of Secretaries General of OPEC"). The conference ordinarily meets at the Vienna headquarters, at least twice a year and in additional extraordinary sessions when necessary. It generally operates on the principles of unanimity and "one member, one vote", with each country paying an equal membership fee into the annual budget.[[19]](#cite_note-statute-19) However, since Saudi Arabia is by far the largest and most-profitable oil exporter in the world, with enough capacity to function as the traditional [swing producer](/wiki/Swing_producer "Swing producer") to balance the global market, it serves as "OPEC's *de facto* leader".[[20]](#cite_note-FT2015-20)

[Domestic cats](/wiki/Cat "Cat") have been diversified by humans into [breeds](/wiki/Breed "Breed") and [domestic and wild hybrids](/wiki/Felid_hybrid "Felid hybrid"). Many such breeds are recognized by various [cat registries](/wiki/Cat_registry "Cat registry"). Additionally, there are new and experimental breeds, [landraces](/wiki/Landrace "Landrace") being established as standardized breeds, distinct domestic populations not being actively developed and lapsed (extinct) breeds.

As of 2023, [the International Cat Association](/wiki/The_International_Cat_Association "The International Cat Association") (TICA) recognizes 75 standardized breeds,[[1]](#cite_note-1) the [Cat Fanciers' Association](/wiki/Cat_Fanciers%27_Association "Cat Fanciers' Association") (CFA) recognizes 45,[[2]](#cite_note-2) the [Fédération Internationale Féline](/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_F%C3%A9line "Fédération Internationale Féline") (FIFe) recognizes 50,[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-fife_list_of_breeds-4) the [Governing Council of the Cat Fancy](/wiki/Governing_Council_of_the_Cat_Fancy "Governing Council of the Cat Fancy") (GCCF) recognizes 45,[[5]](#cite_note-gccf_breeds_registered_2022-5) and the [World Cat Federation](/wiki/World_Cat_Federation "World Cat Federation") (WCF) recognizes 69.[[6]](#cite_note-wcf_breeds_recognized-6)

Inconsistency in a breed's classification and naming among registries means that an individual animal may be considered different breeds by different registries (though not necessarily eligible for registry in them all, depending on its exact ancestry). Bol and [Gheorghe Mureșan](/wiki/Gheorghe_Mure%C8%99an "Gheorghe Mureșan") are the two tallest players in the history of the NBA.[[45]](#cite_note-Brown-46) Official NBA publications have listed Bol at either 7 ft 6 in (2.29 m)[[2]](#cite_note-MBNBA-2) or 7 ft 7 in (2.31 m)[[3]](#cite_note-NBAencyc-3) tall. He was measured by the [Guinness Book of World Records](/wiki/Guinness_Book_of_World_Records "Guinness Book of World Records") at 7 ft 6 3⁄4 in tall.[[46]](#cite_note-47) Complementing his great height, Bol had exceptionally long limbs (inseam 49 inches (120 cm)) and large hands and feet ([size](/wiki/Shoe_size "Shoe size") 16 1/2). His [arm span](/wiki/Arm_span "Arm span"), at 8 feet 6 inches (2.59 m), is (as of 2023) the longest in NBA history, and his upward reach was 10 feet 5 inches (3.18 m).[[47]](#cite_note-WaPo_obit-48)[[48]](#cite_note-49)

With his great height and very long limbs, Bol was one of the NBA's most imposing defensive presences. Along with setting the rookie shot-blocking record in 1985–86, Bol later tied the NBA record for most blocked shots in one half (11) and in one quarter (eight, twice).[[49]](#cite_note-50) On January 31, 1992, in a game against the [Orlando Magic](/wiki/Orlando_Magic "Orlando Magic"), he blocked four consecutive shots in a single possession.[[50]](#cite_note-FSN-51) On average, he blocked one shot per every 5.6 minutes of playing time.[[43]](#cite_note-SI_01-44)
Bol's other basketball skills, however, were very limited. His rail-thin physique made it difficult for him to establish position against the league's bulkier centers and power forwards, and he also suffered from a [claw hand](/wiki/Ulnar_claw "Ulnar claw") on his right hand (his natural hand), which severely affected his shooting and ball-handling abilities. To compensate for this inherited deformity on his right hand, Bol learned to dribble, block shots and rebound with his (non-dominant) left hand.[[51]](#cite_note-52)

Off the court, Bol established a reputation as a practical joker; Charles Barkley, a frequent victim of his pranks, has attested to Bol's sense of humor.[[52]](#cite_note-53

On 27 January 2011, Lenovo formed a joint venture to produce personal computers with Japanese electronics firm [NEC](/wiki/NEC "NEC"). The companies said in a statement that they would establish a new company called Lenovo NEC Holdings, to be registered in the Netherlands. NEC received US$175 million in Lenovo stock. Lenovo was to own a 51% stake in the joint venture, while NEC would have 49%. Lenovo has a five-year option to expand its stake in the joint venture.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

This joint venture was intended to boost Lenovo's worldwide sales by expanding its presence in Japan, a key market for personal computers. NEC spun off its personal computer business into the joint venture. As of 2010, NEC controlled about 20% of Japan's market for personal computers while Lenovo had a 5% share. Lenovo and NEC also agreed to explore cooperating in other areas such as servers and tablet computers.[[41]](#cite_note-41)

Roderick Lappin, chairman of the Lenovo–NEC joint venture, told the press that the two companies will expand their co-operation to include the development of tablet computers.[[42]](#cite_note-ET-42)

In June 2011, Lenovo announced that it planned to acquire control of [Medion](/wiki/Medion "Medion"), a German electronics manufacturing company. Lenovo said the acquisition would double its share of the German computer market, making it the third-largest vendor by sales (after [Acer](/wiki/Acer_Inc. "Acer Inc.") and [Hewlett-Packard](/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard")). The deal, which closed in the third quarter of the same year, was claimed by *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* as "the first in which a Chinese company acquired a well-known German company."[[43]](#cite_note-Kraut-43)

This acquisition gave Lenovo 14% of the German computer market. Gerd Brachmann, chairman of Medion, agreed to sell two-thirds of his 60 per cent stake in the company. He was paid in cash for 80 per cent of the shares and received 20 per cent in Lenovo stock. That gave him about one percent of Lenovo.[[43]](#cite_note-Kraut-43)
